blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
The quantum invariant for the 3-manifold $\mathcal{M}$ was introduced as a path integral on $\mathcal{M}$ by Witten [@EWitt89a]; as the $SU(2)$ invariant we have $$\label{Witten}
  Z_{k} (\mathcal{M})
  =
  \int \exp\Bigl(
    2 \, \pi \, \mathrm{i} \, k \,
    \mathop{\mathrm{CS}}(A)
  \Bigr) \,
  \mathcal{D} A$$ where $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, and $\mathop{\mathrm{CS}}(A)$ is the Chern--Simons functional defined by $$\mathop{\mathrm{CS}}(A)=
  \frac{1}{8 \, \pi^2} \,
  \int\limits_{\mathcal{M}}
  \mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}
  \left(
    A \wedge \mathrm{d} A +
    \frac{2}{3} \, A \wedge A \wedge A
  \ri

blocks.title: The Eichler Integral and the Chern--Simons Invariant
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:Eichler label="sec:Eichler"}

The Eichler integral was originally defined as a $k-1$-fold integration of a modular form with integral weight $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$ (see, *e.g.*, Ref. ). Following Refs.  (see also Refs. ), we define the Eichler integral of the modular form $\Phi_{\boldsymbol{p}}^{(\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3)}(\tau)$ with *half-integral* weight $3/2$ by $$\widetilde{\Phi}_{\boldsymbol{p}}^{(\ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3)}(\tau)
  =
  \sum_{n=0}^\infty
  \chi_{2 P}^{(\ell_1 , \ell_2, \ell_3)}(n) \,
  q^{\frac{n^2}{4 P}}$$

blocks.title: The Witten--Reshetikhin--Turaev Invariant and the Eichler Integral
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:WRT label="sec:WRT"}

We have shown that the Eichler integral at $\tau\to N \in \mathbb{Z}$ gives the Chern--Simons invariant of the Brieskorn homology spheres $\Sigma(p_1,p_2,p_3)$. We shall show that the WRT invariant for the Brieskorn homology spheres can be expressed in terms of a limiting value of the Eichler integral at $\tau\to 1/N$ which is given in eq. [\[Eichler_fraction\]](#Eichler_fraction){reference-type="eqref" reference="Eichler_fraction"}.

blocks.title: Discussions
blocks.content:
We have studied the Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant for the Brieskorn homology
spheres (2.11) by use of properties of the Eichler integral of the half-integral weight based on
the method of Ref. 23. The WRT invariant coincides with a limiting value of the Eichler integral at
τ →1/N for N ∈Z, and the nearly modular property (4.17) of the Eichler integral gives an exact
